source.what: Joby Aviation news index (the Newsroom listing page) — the archive that the single-article rubric's 'Read next' band links into. A full rubric covering all seven aspects.
source.method: Chromium (ms-playwright chromium-1234) driven by puppeteer-core, one isolated browser context per width. Viewports 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844 at deviceScaleFactor 1. Each pass scrolled once through the document, then every running animation was finished and its styles committed so nothing measured was in a hidden state; the last animation running at that point is the list's fade-in. Cookie overlays were removed before measurement. Values are getComputedStyle and getBoundingClientRect readings plus resolved :root custom properties and CSS rule text read out of the document stylesheets. Card and track geometry is read from live boxes, not inferred.
gaps: Category filtering was not exercised. The page has a two-item category list (Blog Posts, Press Releases) but clicking either was out of scope, so the filtered state, its transition and whether the list is re-laid-out are unmeasured. The 'listFade' animation (300ms, linear) is captured as it runs on load and is the mechanism that would carry a filter change, but that is inference.

The category hover state could not be confirmed. Hovering 'Press Releases' produced no change in colour, opacity, font-size or transform on either the link or its first child, which most likely means the hover affordance lives on a different descendant or is driven by a transition not sampled at the right element. Recorded as unconfirmed rather than as 'no hover state'.

Cross-page card alignment is measured only within this page: all eleven regular items share an identical height (211.8px) and identical internal geometry here. Whether that holds when a headline runs to five lines instead of two was not tested, because the listing carries a fixed set of articles.

The 13-track inner grid was resolved as a track count and gap but its intended reading was not confirmed against the site's own spec. The outer 16-track grid comes from --grid-columns on :root; the inner 13-track grid appears only in the component styles, with no token backing it.

The featured item's image-to-text relationship could not be fully resolved: the featured image container is 621.6px tall against a 1.78:1 ratio, but whether the ratio is authored or a consequence of the image's own dimensions was not isolated.

The media kit band's background rises 690px above its own section box (section y 4192 h 1090, but its image starts at y 3652), so the band overlaps the preceding section. Whether that overlap is intentional composition or a layout collision was not resolved, and it is recorded as an open question rather than as a defect.
The page's list has no pagination or load-more control; all eleven items plus the featured article render at once. Whether the listing is truncated server-side at this count was not determined.
Motion at 834 and 390 was not sampled per element; entrance values come from the 1440 pass and the page's shared keyframe library.
The nav and footer are site-wide components with their own rubrics (joby_nav_v1.json, joby_footer_v1.json) and are described here only as they appear on this page.
The article count and any 'showing N of M' behaviour was not verified against the CMS.
source.notes: This page is the archive view of the same publication as the single-article page, and it breaks the parent system in a different place. The outer chrome is the parent 16-track grid with the parent 16px gap and 40px gutter, unchanged. But every card row is a 13-track grid with a 12px gap — a second, undocumented column system that appears in the component styles and has no root token. Worse, that 13-track grid is sized to its own container (1105px) rather than to the page band, so the cards' right edge lands at x 1400 while the sidebar and the page gutter sit on tracks measured from a different origin. The listing therefore has two grids whose columns do not share a scale: 16 tracks of 70px with 16px gaps outside, 13 tracks of 73.92px with 12px gaps inside. Recorded alongside are three further points: the section gap between featured and list items is zero (the divider rule does the separating), the category rail is 255px and never sticky, and the featured title uses -2% tracking where every other display size on the parent uses -3%.

parts.name: Parent 16-track chrome around a list
parts.description: The page header, the listing section and the footer all sit on the parent 16-track grid with the parent 16px gap and 40px gutter — the same system the article page uses. The page header places its title at column 1 and the listing section reserves its left columns for a category rail.
parts.entry_test: Replace the chrome's grid with the list's own and the page header stops agreeing with every other page on the site; the shared outer grid is what makes this page recognisably part of the same publication.
parts.recipe: Consume the parent grid in every chrome element: 16 tracks, column-gap 16px, padding 0 40px at 1440. The hero content is a 16-track grid measuring 1368px wide with a 16px gap; the listing section is a 16-track grid with padding 0 40px 120px; the footer is the same 16-track grid it is everywhere. Do not let the chrome inherit the list's inner grid — the two systems serve different jobs and the list's must not leak outward.

checks.check: Page header, listing section and footer all resolve to the parent 16-track grid
The parent gap and gutter are unchanged from other pages
The page title sits at the parent grid's first column
The listing section reserves track columns for the rail rather than floating it
No chrome element inherits the list's inner grid

measured: listsSection display grid, padding '0px 40px 120px', box x 0 w 1440
measured: footer 16 tracks, gap 16px, padding '38px 40px 89px' — identical to the article page's footer
--grid-columns resolves to 16 and --base-padding to 4rem at a 10px root, the same tokens as the article page
the hero's first track measures 485.16px because the title spans a substituted track, but the grid still resolves 16 tracks

parts.name: Inner 13-track card grid
parts.description: Every card row — the featured article and all eleven list items — is laid out on a 13-track grid with a 12px gap, distinct from the parent 16-track grid. The track count comes from the component styles, not from a root token. Date, image, title and category are placed by explicit span on those thirteen tracks.
parts.entry_test: Place the card's parts on the parent 16-track grid and the image and title drift out of their columns relative to the divider rule; the 13-track inner grid is what holds the card's internal alignment.
parts.recipe: A nested grid on card content: 13 tracks, column-gap 12px, row-gap 12px. Card parts placed by span — date at span 1, image at 2 / span 3, title at 6 / span 5, category at 13 / span 1. At 1440 the tracks resolve to 73.92px each inside a 1105px container (13 x 73.92 + 12 x 12 = 960.96 + 144 = 1104.96). Critically: do not adopt this page's orphaned second system. A second grid with its own track count is defensible only if it is tokenised and its columns are demonstrably related to the outer grid's; here it is neither. The corrected contract is either to place card parts on the parent 16 tracks, or to declare the inner grid as a named token and state how its 13 tracks map to the outer 16.

checks.check: Card parts are placed by explicit span rather than by content width
The inner grid's track count is declared as a token, not hard-coded in a component
The inner grid's columns bear a stated relationship to the outer grid
The inner grid's own arithmetic closes against its container
The same inner grid is used by the featured row and the list rows

parts.name: Rows separated by a rule, not by space
parts.description: List items are separated by a 1px full-width rule rather than by a gap: successive items measure zero distance apart, and the only thing dividing them is an absolutely positioned hairline sitting exactly on the boundary. The rule is the ink at 20% alpha, so it reads as a soft grey rather than a hard line.
parts.entry_test: Remove the rule and eleven items merge into one undifferentiated column, because there is no space between them at all; the hairline is doing the entire job of separation.
parts.recipe: Each item is position relative, and carries an absolutely positioned 1px rule element at its top edge, spanning the full width of the list container (1105px) in the ink colour at 20% alpha. Item padding is 16px top and 32px bottom, asymmetric, with no top border. Because the rule is absolutely positioned, it does not consume layout height — which is why successive items measure zero gap. Keep the rule full-width across the list, and keep the padding on the item rather than as margins between items, so the rule sits exactly on the boundary.

checks.check: List items are divided by a rule rather than by a gap
The rule spans the full width of the list container
The rule is soft (a tint of the ink) rather than a solid hard line
The rule does not consume layout height
Every item carries the rule, including the first

evidence: measured: eleven borderLineBase rules, each 1px tall, x 295 w 1105, background rgba(14,22,32,0.2), position absolute
successive item gaps measure 0px on all seven pairs sampled
item computed padding '16px 0px 32px' — asymmetric, and the item carries no top border
the rule's 1105px width equals the list container's width exactly

parts.name: Featured article leads the list
parts.description: The list opens with one featured article: a full-width image band above a two-part text row, its date at column 1 and its title spanning columns 6 to 12 — the same 13-track grid the smaller items use, at a much larger scale, so it sets the page's entry point.
parts.entry_test: Open the list with an ordinary item and the page has no entry point; the featured article's full-width image is what establishes the hierarchy.
parts.recipe: The featured item spans the full 16-column grid, with a 1 / -1 image container above and a text row beneath it. The image container is 1105px wide and 621.6px tall (1.78:1). The text row is a 13-track grid with 26px top and bottom padding, placing the date at span 1 (85px track) and the title at 6 / span 7 (607px). Title type is 40px/500 in the display face with tight leading. The item carries 120px of bottom padding, which is the only separation between it and the first list item besides that item's rule.

checks.check: Exactly one item is treated as featured and leads the list
The featured image spans the full width of the list container
The featured title is set larger than any list item title
The featured text row uses the same inner grid as the list rows
The featured title spans more columns than a list item title

parts.name: Item anatomy: date, image, title, category
parts.description: Every list item has the same five parts in the same columns: a date in the first column, the image across columns 2 to 4, the title across columns 6 to 10, and the category in the last column — with empty columns reserved between the image and the title, and between the title and the category, so the parts read as four separate registers rather than one run.
parts.entry_test: Run the parts together and an item becomes a line of text with a picture; the reserved empty columns are what let the eye separate date, image, title and category without any labels or rules.
parts.recipe: Four parts on the 13-track inner grid: date at span 1; image at 2 / span 3; title at 6 / span 5; category at 13 / span 1. Note the two reserved gaps — column 5 sits empty between the image and the title, and columns 11 and 12 sit empty between the title and the category. At 1440 that is 73.9 + 245.8 + [empty 73.9] + 417.6 + [empty 147.8] + 73.9 across the 1105px. Date and category are set at the caption size in the text face; the title is 20px/500. All four parts share the item's top edge and its 163.8px content height.

parts.name: Date pinned to the first column
parts.description: The date sits alone in the leftmost column of every item, set at the caption size, and its column is only as wide as a caption needs — so the date forms a narrow labelled margin down the left of the whole list, and the eye can scan it as a column of its own.
parts.entry_test: Move the date beside the title and the list loses its left margin; the dedicated first column is what makes eleven items scannable by date.
parts.recipe: The date occupies span 1 of the inner 13-track grid — a single track, 73.9px at 1440 — at the caption size (12px/450) in the text face, top-aligned with the rest of the item. It does not wrap to multiple lines at the desktop width. Because every item uses the same first-column span, the dates form an aligned column down the page; this is the list's only vertical guide besides the divider rules.

parts.name: Category in the last column
parts.description: The category sits alone in the rightmost column of every item, at the same caption size and weight as the date, so each item is bracketed by two small labels — when it was published on the left, what it is on the right — with the image and headline held between them.
parts.entry_test: Drop the category and the list loses its right-hand rail; the paired small labels are what frame each row.
parts.recipe: The category occupies span 1 of the inner grid at its end — column 13, 73.9px at 1440 — at the caption size (12px/450) in the text face, sharing the item's top edge. Use the same type spec as the date so the two read as a matched pair, and leave columns 11 and 12 empty so the category is separated from the title by a clear gap rather than sitting beside it.

parts.name: Category rail beside the list
parts.description: A narrow rail on the left of the listing holds the category filters as a plain stack of text, unboxed and unfilled, matching the list's left rail so the rail's first item aligns with the page's list column.
parts.entry_test: Make the rail a row of pills above the list and it competes with the featured article; the quiet left stack is what keeps filtering available without becoming the page's subject.
parts.recipe: A rail 255px wide at x 40 — the parent grid's first columns — beside a list container 1105px wide at x 295. The rail holds each category as a block of text at body size in the text face, with 12px between them, no background, no border and no radius. The rail is not sticky: it scrolls away with the page while the list beside it is far taller (255px of rail against a 3397px list). The rail's own top (y 675) matches the list container's top exactly, so the first category aligns with the featured item's top edge.

parts.name: Two caption rails framing each row
parts.description: The date and the category are set at the same small size, the same weight and the same tracking, so they read as a matched pair of labels framing every item. Their size is the page's caption step, two steps below the item title and three below the featured title.
parts.entry_test: Set the date and category at different sizes and the framing breaks; the matched spec is what makes the two rails read as one system.
parts.recipe: One shared caption style used by both the date and the category: 12px, weight 450, line-height 14.4px, letter-spacing -0.24px, in the text face, no transform. It is the same caption step used across the site's other pages, so the rails stay in the parent's type system even though the items sit on their own grid.

parts.name: The list fades as a whole
parts.description: The whole list is wrapped in a fade layer that animates in over 300ms, so the eleven items and the featured article arrive together as one surface rather than as a cascade. The same layer is the mechanism that would carry a category filter change.
parts.entry_test: Fade each item separately and the list staggers; the single wrapper is what makes a long list read as one object arriving.
parts.recipe: Wrap the entire list in a single element that carries one fade animation — 300ms, linear — rather than attaching an entrance to each item. On this page the wrapper is a plain div around the list, and the animation is captured running on load. Images inside carry their own separate 400ms fade, so the wrapper's fade and the images' fades are independent.

parts.name: Closing media kit band
parts.description: Below the listing sits a full-bleed closing band with a title on the left and a supporting line on the right, plus a single call to action — the page's only promotional surface, and the only place on this page where text is reversed out on a dark ground.
parts.entry_test: End the page on the last list item and the archive just stops; the media kit band is what closes it and turns a list into a destination.
parts.recipe: A full-bleed band with a background image, padding 150px 40px 40px. Title at 48px/500 in the display face, reversed out in the light token, placed on the left (x 40 w 586); a supporting paragraph at 14px/400 on the right (x 1072 w 328); and one call-to-action beneath the title. Note this page's band background rises 690px above the band's own top edge, overlapping the section before it — treat that as an unresolved question, not a pattern to copy. Keep the band full-bleed and keep the title and supporting copy on the outer rails, not centred.

parts.name: Weight carries the hierarchy
parts.description: Every step in the listing's hierarchy is carried by weight and size together, in half-hundred steps — 450 for the caption rails, 500 for titles, 550 for the page title. Nothing is bold, nothing is below 400, and no step relies on colour or case to distinguish itself.
parts.entry_test: Set the page title and item titles at one weight and the hierarchy flattens into a list of same-looking rows; the weight steps are what let size alone carry the difference.
parts.recipe: Use the parent's closed weight set: 400 body, 450 caption rails, 500 titles, 550 page title and display. No uppercase anywhere on the page, and no colour change to mark a level — every string is the same ink token. Tracking stays proportional to size: -3% at 100px, -2% at 40px, -6% on the 20px item title, -2% at 12px.

parts.name: One scale that rescales, not resteps
parts.description: The page's type and grid both rescale proportionally below the desktop widths rather than stepping: the page title runs 100px at 1440, 81.44px at 834 and 49.92px at 390, all by the same fluid factor, and the caption runs 12, 9.77 and 10.4 on the same curve. The grid changes track count at the smallest width while the type keeps its ratio.
parts.entry_test: Step the type at breakpoints and the page's rhythm jolts at each one; the proportional rescale is what keeps one scale working from 390 to 1440.
parts.recipe: Drive type and track sizes from a fluid root rather than from per-breakpoint values. The root measures 10px at 1440, 8.14px at 834 and 10.4px at 390, and every type size is a rem multiple of that root — which is why the same nominal sizes appear at every width with different computed values. Hold the display-to-caption ratio across all three widths. At the smallest width the grid restructures (the outer grid drops to 6 tracks and the inner to 6) while the type ratio is preserved.

parts.name: Card images share one ratio
parts.description: Every list item's image is exactly the same size and ratio — 245.8 by 163.8px, a 1.5:1 crop — so the eleven images form a clean column down the page. The featured image above them is a different ratio (1.78:1) by design, at full width.
parts.entry_test: Let each image take its natural ratio and the list's image column develops ragged edges; the single crop ratio is what makes eleven rows align.
parts.recipe: Crop every list item image to the same 3:2 ratio at a fixed size (245.8 x 163.8px at 1440, inside a three-track span), with object-fit cover and an 8px border radius. Crop the featured image to 1.78:1 at full list width with radius 0. Note the parent article page's card row fails exactly this test — three cards with three different ratios — so the index page's consistency is the behaviour worth taking, not the article page's.

parts.name: The list renders whole
parts.description: The archive renders every item at once with no pagination, no load-more control and no infinite-scroll trigger visible. The list is a single block on the page, ending at the closing band.
parts.entry_test: Add a pager and the list acquires a second navigation problem on a page that already has a category rail; rendering the set whole keeps the archive a single visual statement.
parts.recipe: Render the full list inside one grid element with no paging affordance. On this page the articles grid holds twelve children (one featured plus eleven regular) in a single 3324px block, and no control matching load-more, next, previous or page patterns exists. Whether the count is capped server-side is unresolved; the observable contract is that the page presents its list as one unit.

limitations: Category filtering is unmeasured. The rail's two filters were not exercised, so the filtered state, its transition and any re-layout of the list are unknown. The listFade animation (300ms) is captured on load and is the likely carrier, but that is inference.

The category hover state could not be confirmed. Hovering 'Press Releases' produced no change in colour, opacity, font-size or transform on the link or its first child. This is recorded as unconfirmed rather than as an absent hover state — the affordance may live on a descendant not sampled.

Two grid systems coexist and the inner one is a defect, not a target. The chrome sits on the parent 16-track grid; every card row sits on a 13-track grid with a 12px gap that has no root token and no stated relationship to the 16. The rubric requires the second system to be tokenised and mapped.

Type tracking is inconsistent on this page and is recorded as such. The parent's rule is -3% of size (with a -2% exception at 12px); this page runs -2.4% at 100px, -3% at 48px, -2% at 40px and 14px, -2% at 12px, and -6% on the 20px item title. The -6% item-title value is an outlier.
The list image crop breaks at the smallest width: 1.5:1 at 1440 and 834, but 1.07:1 (effectively square) at 390. Whether that is deliberate or a consequence of the container is unresolved.

The closing band's background image rises 690px above its own section box (section y 4192, image y 3652), so it overlaps the preceding section. Recorded as an open question, not as a defect or a pattern.

Cross-page card consistency is only verified within this page. All eleven items share an identical 211.8px height here because the listing's headlines happen to wrap to similar lengths; the layout's behaviour with a much longer headline was not tested.
The 13-track inner grid's intended reading was not confirmed against the site's own specification. It appears only in component styles with no token backing it.
The featured item's image ratio (1.78:1) is measured but whether it is authored or a consequence of the source image's dimensions was not isolated.
The page renders all twelve items with no paging control; whether the listing is capped server-side was not determined.
Motion at 834 and 390 was not sampled per element; values come from the 1440 pass and the shared keyframe library.
The nav and footer are site-wide components with their own rubrics and are not re-graded here.
